::: {#background-goal .section .level1}
# Background & Goal

Having optimized the FungaLight assay in *C. glabrata* under hydrogen
peroxide treatment and compared its result to CFU, we would like to test
its applicability beyond this single species. To do so, Hanxi applied
FungaLight to *S. cerevisiae* and *C. albicans*, two other commonly used
yeast species, also treated with hydrogen peroxide, and compared the
results to CFU. Because the three species have different basal
resistance to hydrogen peroxide, a different concentration series were
used.

The experiments for *S. cerevisiae* were conducted on 2024.02.25-28, and
for *C. albicans* on 20240318-23. Post-treatment cells were stained with
PI or PI+SYTO9 (=FungaLight), and run through flow cytometry. The same
sample was also plated for CFU.

This notebook will focus on the *S. cerevisiae* data.
:::

::: {#import-data .section .level1}
# Import data

> FCS files are stored in rdss/Users/Hanxi/flow cytometry under the
> above dates. They are copied to this repository under the same names.

*note*: samples are labeled by the H2O2 doses they were treated with.
`_b` in the filename indicates the sample was stained with both PI and
SYTO9, i.e., FungaLight, while `_p` indicates PI alone.

``` r
# use relative path to make it easier for collaboration
data.path = "../input/20240225-28-h2o2-log-Sc-FGL/"
dat0 <- read.flowSet(path = data.path, pattern = "*.fcs",
                     transformation = FALSE,  # the original values are already linearized. 
                     emptyValue = FALSE,  alter.names = TRUE,   # change parameter names to R format
                     column.pattern = ".H|FSC|SSC") # only load the height variables for the fluorescent parameters
```

Simplify the sample names

``` r
oriNames <- sampleNames(dat0)
tmp <- str_split(oriNames, pattern = "_", simplify = TRUE)[,c(1, 5, 6)]
colnames(tmp) <- c("Date", "Treatment", "Dye")
treatment.levels <- c("5C", "0", "0.6", "6", "1000")
sample <- data.frame(tmp) %>% 
  mutate(
    Dye = ifelse(Dye == "p.fcs", "PI", ifelse(Dye == "b.fcs", "Both", Dye)), 
    Treatment = fct_inorder(Treatment),
    name = paste(Date, 
                 ifelse(Treatment == "1000", "1M", paste0(Treatment, "mM")), 
                 Dye, sep = "_")
  )
rownames(sample) <- oriNames
dat <- dat0 # make a copy
pData(dat) <- sample
write_tsv(pData(dat), file = "../input/20240225-log-h2o2-sc-sample.tsv")
```
:::

::: {#gating-for-singlets .section .level2}
## Gating for singlets

> The following gaphing steps are used to gate singlets by FSC and SSC
> values. Only singlets are included in analysis. Gate for outlier

``` r
#outlier.gate <- rectangleGate(filterId = "-outlier", "FSC.H" = c(1.2e5, 1e6), "SSC.H" = c(1e2, 1e6))
ggcyto(dat[1], aes(x = FSC.H, y = SSC.H), subset = "root") +
  geom_hex(bins = 64) + geom_gate(outlier.gate) + facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 2) + ggcyto_par_set(limits = "instrument")
```

    Coordinate system already present. Adding new coordinate system, which will
    replace the existing one.

![](data:image/png;base64,){role="img"}

Add gate to GS

``` r
gs <- GatingSet(dat) # create a GatingSet
# rename the samples
sampleNames(gs) <- pData(gs)$name
# repair the Date column in pData
pData(gs)$Date = paste0("0", pData(gs)$Date)
# add the outlier gate
gs_pop_add(gs, outlier.gate, parent = "root")
```

::: {#gate-for-live-cells .section .level2}
## Gate for live cells

This is the live population with red fluorescence below 10\^2.2

> **Main takeaway**
>
> 1.  From 10mM to 1M treated samples, %live decreases and the change is
>     much more obvious in the dual stain (PI first or simultaneous)
>     than PI alone
>
> 2.  The mock treated sample has a visible high red high green (not as
>     high and prominent as the 100 mM treated) than 10 mM treated. It
>     doesn't follow the trend above.

``` r
scPars <- ggcyto_par_set(limits = list(x = c(0,10^5.5), y = c(0,10^5.5)))
#polygon <- matrix(c(0, 5*10^3, 5*10^3, 0, # BL1.H, green
#                    10^2.2, 10^2.2, 0, 0),# BL3.H, red
#                  ncol = 2)
#colnames(polygon) <- c("BL1.H", "BL3.H")
#live.gate <- polygonGate(filterId = "live", .gate = polygon)
p.axis <- list(
  scale_x_logicle(breaks = 10^c(2,3,4,5)),
  scale_y_logicle(breaks = 10^c(2,3,4,5)),
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1.1), face = 2)
  )
)
for(date in c("022524", "022624", "022824")){
  p <- ggcyto(gs[pData(gs)$Date == date], aes(x = BL1.H, y = BL3.H), subset = "singlet") + 
    geom_hex(bins = 128) + 
    geom_gate(live.gate.sc) + 
    geom_stats(location = "gate", adjust = c(0.02, 2), digits = 1, ) + 
    labs(title = paste0("Date: ", date)) +
    facet_grid(Dye ~ factor(Treatment, levels = treatment.levels)) +# scPars +
    p.axis
  print(p)
}
```

::: {#gate-for-the-intermediate-population-with-high-syto9 .section .level2}
## Gate for the intermediate population with high SYTO9

This is the intermediate population with high Red and Green. We
hypothesize that they represent oxidatively damaged cells with partially
compromised plasma membranes, resulting in more SYTO9 accumulation but
not a significant increase in PI.

``` r

#                    10^2.2, 10^2.2, 10^4), ncol = 2)
#polygon <- matrix(c(10^3, 10^5.5, 10^5.5,   # BL1.H, green

  p <- ggcyto(gs[pData(gs)$Date == date], aes(x = BL1.H, y = BL3.H),
              subset = "singlet") + 
    geom_hex(bins = 128) + 
    geom_gate(inter.gate.sc) + 
    geom_stats(location = "data",  adjust = c(0.05, 5), digits = 3) +
```

::: {#representative-fgl-staining-pattern .section .level2}
## Representative FGL staining pattern

We have demonstrated our general gating strategy in Figure 4. Here, the
goal is to show an example of the FGL staining pattern applied to other
species. For *C. albicans* in particular, there are some notable
differences that required us to adjust the gate boundaries. We will skip
PI alone staining for brevity and only show one replicate.

``` r
scPars <- ggcyto_par_set(limits = list(x = c(0,10^5), y = c(0,10^4.2)))
treatment_labels <- c(
  "0" = "0 mM", "0.6" = "0.6 mM", "6" = "6 mM", "1000" = "1M"
)
p <- ggcyto(gs[with(pData(gs), 
                    Date == "022824" & Dye == "Both" & Treatment != "5C")], 
            aes(x = BL1.H, y = BL3.H), subset = "singlet") + 
  geom_hex(bins = 128) + 
  geom_gate(live.gate.sc, colour = "gray20") + 
  geom_gate(inter.gate.sc, colour = "steelblue3") + 
  #geom_stats(location = "gate", adjust = c(0.02, 2), digits = 1, fill = NA) + 
  facet_grid(. ~ factor(Treatment, levels = names(treatment_labels), 
                        labels = treatment_labels)) + 
  scPars + p.axis +
  theme(plot.title = element_blank(), axis.title = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = rel(0.8), face = 2))
```

::: {#explore-cell-size-difference-in-hydrogen-peroxide-treated-cells .section .level2}
## Explore cell size difference in hydrogen peroxide treated cells

This is based on Jinye's suggestion: \> I am wondering is whether the
cell size and granularity would affect the staining in different ways
among species. Thus, I think it makes sense to plot the FL on FSC or SSC
and perform a linear regression analysis for each species, if there is
no significant difference, we can say the cell property of different
species does not affect the staining in different ways. This is a
simplified or adapted idea from PMID: 21952134.

Let's plot the distribution of FSC.H as a proxy for cell size

``` r
mult_format <- function() {
     function(x) format(x/10000,digits = 2) 
}
```

``` r
subset <- with(pData(gs), Treatment != "5C")
p1 <- ggcyto(gs[subset], aes(x = FSC.H), subset = "singlet") + 
  ggridges::geom_density_ridges(
    aes(y = factor(Treatment, levels = treatment.levels)),
        fill = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels = mult_format(), name = "FSC.H x 10000") +
    facet_grid(Date ~ Dye) + labs(title = NULL)
p1
ggsave("../output/20250310-Sc-log-h2o2-cell-size-distribution-compare.png",
       width = 4, height = 4)
```

![](data:image/png;base64,){role="img"}
:::

::: {#extract-gated-stats-and-mfi .section .level1}
# Extract gated stats and MFI

\% of events in each of the three gates

``` r
# we are only interested in the populations after singlet gating
nodes <- c("singlet", "intermediate", "live")
# get the event count
gated_cnt <- gs_pop_get_stats(gs, nodes, type = "count")
# get the MFI for each parameter in each population of interest
gated_mfi <- gs_pop_get_stats(gs, nodes, type = pop.MFI) %>% 
  select(sample, pop, starts_with("FungaLight"))
```

Combine the data and meta data

``` r
gated_stats <- full_join(gated_cnt, gated_mfi, by = c("sample", "pop")) %>% 
  right_join(pData(gs), by = c("sample" = "name")) %>% 
  relocate(Date, Treatment, Dye, .after = sample) %>% 
  relocate(sample, .after = last_col())
write_tsv(gated_stats, file = "../output/20250310-Sc-log-h2o2-gated-stats.tsv")

# we don't need the MFI for the latter analysis. add meta data to gated_cnt
gated_freq <- left_join(sample, gated_cnt, by = c("name" = "sample")) %>% 
  select(-name) %>% 
  group_by(Date, Treatment, Dye) %>% 
  mutate(perc = count / count[pop == "singlet"], .after = count)
```

:::::::: {#compare-with-cfu .section .level1}
# Compare with CFU

::: {#read-cfu-data .section .level2}
## Read CFU data

These are averaged CFU provided by Hanxi. Here are the raw cfu data

``` r
cfu_raw <- read_tsv("../input/20240225-0323-h2o2-Sc-Ca-CFU-raw.tsv",
                    col_types = "cccccciiii", comment = "#")
cfu_calc <- cfu_raw %>% 
  select(Date, Species, Treatment = H2O2_mM, Group, Dilution, Raw_count = Total) %>% 
  mutate(Date = ymd(Date) |> format("%m%d%y"),
         Treatment = fct_inseq(Treatment),
         CFU = Dilution * Raw_count) %>% 
  # group by Date to calculate the ratio of MO to MM
  group_by(Date) %>% 
  mutate(p_live = CFU / CFU[Group == "MM"]) %>% 
  # retain only Sc data
  dplyr::filter(Species == "Sc")

# export the data for paper
# write_tsv(cfu_calc, file = "../output/20250315-Sc-Ca-h2o2-cfu-estimate.tsv")
```
:::

::: {#calculate-survival-from-pi-alone-or-fungalight .section .level2}
## Calculate survival from PI alone or FungaLight

For both PI alone and FungaLight, we will calculate the percent live
events. For FungaLight specifically, we will also record the percent
intermediate events and will investigate its utility

``` r
dye_based <- gated_freq %>% 
  # record the total number of events as the count of singlets
  group_by(Date, Treatment, Dye) %>% 
  mutate(total_event_count = count[pop == "singlet"]) %>% 
  # now we don't need the singlet population and the count variable
  select(-count) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(pop != "singlet") %>%
  #ungroup() %>% 
  # we will pivot this data frame to a wider format, making 
  # two new variables out of the percentage variable
  pivot_wider(names_from = pop, values_from = perc, names_prefix = "p_") %>% 
  mutate(p_dead = 1 - p_live - p_intermediate) %>% 
  relocate(p_live, .after = total_event_count)

# export the data for paper
write_tsv(dye_based, file = "../output/20250314-Sc-h2o2-fgl-estimate.tsv")
```

    PI <- final %>% 
      dplyr::filter(Dye == "PI") %>% 
      select(Date, Treatment, Method = Dye, Score = p_live)

    FGL <- final %>% 
      dplyr::filter(Dye == "Both") %>% 
      mutate(
        wFGL = p_live * 2/log(BL1_live, 10)
      ) %>% 
      select(Date, Treatment, wFGL, FGL = p_live) %>% 
      pivot_longer(cols = c(wFGL, FGL), names_to = "Method", values_to = "Score")
      

    all <- bind_rows(
      PI, FGL,
      mutate(cfu, Method = "CFU") %>% rename(Score = CFU)
    ) 

Combine the dye based results with cfu

``` r
cfu_dye <- bind_rows(
  cfu_calc |> #dplyr::filter(Species == "Sc") |>
    mutate(Method = "CFU") |> 
    select(Date, Treatment, Method, p_live),
  select(dye_based, Date, Treatment, Method = Dye, starts_with("p"))) %>% 
  mutate(
    Method = factor(Method, levels = c("CFU", "PI", "Both"),
                    labels = c("CFU", "PI", "FungaLight")),
    Treatment = fct_inorder(Treatment)
  )
```
:::

::: {#plotting-the-results .section .level2}
## Plotting the results

CFU survival

``` r
p.cfu <- cfu_calc %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Species == "Sc") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Treatment, y = p_live)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "summary", fun = "mean", fill = "gray70", width = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = as.character(Date)), 
             position = position_jitter(0.1),
             size = 1.5) + 
  scale_shape_manual(values = 4:6, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, 
                     limits = c(NA, 1.05), breaks = seq(0,1,0.5)) +
  labs(title = "CFU", x = bquote(H[2]*O[2]~(mM)), y = "% Live") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1.2), face = 2),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p.cfu
```

![](data:image/png;base64,){role="img"}

``` r
p.dye <- dye_based %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Treatment != "5C", Dye == "Both") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_inseq(Treatment), y = p_live)) +

  geom_point(aes(shape = as.character(Date)),
```

Alternative bar plots

``` r
p.dye.side_by_side <- dye_based %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Treatment != "5C", Dye == "Both") %>%
  select(Date, Treatment, p_live, p_intermediate) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(p_live, p_intermediate), 
               names_to = "par", values_to = "perc") %>% 
  mutate(par = factor(par, levels = c("p_live", "p_intermediate"),
                      labels = c("% live", "% intermediate"))) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_inseq(Treatment), y = perc, group = par)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = par), position = position_dodge(0.9),
           stat = "summary", fun = "mean", width = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = as.character(Date), color = par), 
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1,
                                             dodge.width = 0.9),
             size = 1.2) + 
  scale_fill_manual(NULL, values = c("gray70", "lightblue2")) +
  scale_color_manual(NULL, values = c("black", "steelblue")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = 4:6, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, 
                     limits = c(NA, 1.05), breaks = seq(0,1,0.5)) +

  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1.2), face = 2),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        legend.position = "inside",
        legend.position.inside = c(0.8, 0.9))
```

Below we use ANOVA and posthoc test to test for significant differences
between the conditions

``` r
#tmp <- dplyr::filter(cfu_dye, Treatment != "5C", Method == "FungaLight") %>% 
#  mutate(Treatment = fct_inseq(Treatment))
#lm <- aov(p_live ~ Treatment, data = tmp)
#TukeyHSD(lm)

cfu_dye %>% ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Treatment != "5C") %>% 
  mutate(Treatment = fct_inseq(Treatment)) %>% 
  select(Treatment, Method, p_live) %>% 
  nest(data = c(Treatment, p_live)) %>% 
  mutate(
    fit = map(data, \(df) aov(p_live ~ Treatment, data = df)),
    posthoc = map(fit, TukeyHSD),
    tidied = map(posthoc, broom::tidy)
  ) %>% 
  unnest(tidied) %>% 
  select(Method, contrast, diff = estimate, lwr = conf.low, upr = conf.high,
         Padj = adj.p.value)
```
